::: {.ter-project-brief}
## Design brief

This **laser name tag** project uses a **teacher-supplied, pre-cut rectangular wood blank**. Create a readable name and original logo or lettermark. The first output is a PNG used for engraving. Keep the first machine experience intentionally simple so attention stays on measuring the real blank, layout, export quality and safe workflow.
:::

## Learning goals

Students distinguish raster artwork from later vector cut geometry, fit artwork to an exact physical size, create visual hierarchy, export a clean PNG, and verify the file before it enters the machine workflow.

## Choose an editing route

**Inkscape (preferred):** use the [editable SVG template](../../assets/laser-library/classroom-kit/name-tag/name-tag-engraving-template.svg), set the page to the measured blank and export the page as PNG.

**Photopea (accessible raster route):** create a new document with the same aspect ratio as the measured blank, place name and original logo on separate layers, maintain a safe margin, then export PNG. Record the intended physical blank size beside the submitted image because a PNG alone does not guarantee physical dimensions.

Study the [three workable layouts and three common problems](../../assets/laser-library/classroom-kit/name-tag/name-tag-layout-examples.svg) before choosing a composition.

## File preparation

1. Measure the supplied blank in millimetres and record width × height.
2. Set the page or canvas to that aspect ratio and physical size.
3. Add the student's name with deliberate typography, spacing and strong contrast.
4. Add the original [logo or lettermark](../02-digital-design/03-logos-lettermarks.qmd).
5. Keep artwork inside the instructor-set safe margin.
6. Remove or hide all guides and export the page, not a loose selection, as PNG.
7. Save the editable master separately from the exported fabrication image.
8. Reopen the PNG and verify crop, orientation, contrast and filename.

## Before pressing start

Follow the local material approval, focus, ventilation, supervision, fire-watch, and shutdown procedure. Confirm the machine job is **engrave only** and that no guide or accidental cut boundary appears.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Useful for **TIJ1O** and **TDJ2O** learning involving vector graphics, visual communication, exact dimensions, file preparation, manufacturing processes, safe tool use, and evaluation of a produced artifact. Communications Technology connections belong primarily in the preceding digital-design unit.
:::

Use the [planning worksheet and classroom toolkit](resources/index.qmd) for this project. Students who are ready for an additional structural problem can continue to the optional [Make It Stand](02-make-it-stand.qmd) extension.
